title: add 'st onboard' to audit a rig for sietch's loop prerequisites
description:
The sietch loop assumes scaffolding the framework doesn't currently verify: pre-commit hooks (so dev-agent commits get auto-formatted before push), GitHub Actions CI (so the agent has a real signal to gate merge on — without it, 'gh pr checks' returns vacuously-green and the agent ships junk), and a test runner with at least one test (so CI's signal is meaningful and the agent's CI-retry loop has something to read from on red).

Today, a user retrofitting sietch onto an existing repo finds out about each missing piece by reading prompt failures or by debugging a silent merge of broken code. 'st onboard' should walk the rig once, report pass/fail per check, and emit copy-pasteable fix snippets for each gap so the user can either fix manually or pipe through bash.
design:
New file: bin/st gains 'onboard' subcommand → calls lib/onboard.sh.

lib/onboard.sh structure:
  - Each check is a named function returning 0/1 + an OK/FAIL printout
  - Functions: check_rig_config, check_beads, check_gh_auth, check_pre_commit_config, check_pre_commit_installed, check_ci_workflow, check_ci_pr_trigger, check_test_dir, check_test_files, check_worktree_base
  - Aggregator runs them all, accumulates pass/fail tally, prints fix snippets for fails
  - Fix snippets live inline in each check function — kept close to the predicate so they don't drift

Output format:
  ✓ rig.config            REPO_SLUG=aniryou/foo
  ✓ .beads/
  ✓ gh auth (aniryou)
  ✗ .pre-commit-config.yaml
      Fix: cat > .pre-commit-config.yaml <<'EOF'
           repos:
             - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
               rev: v0.7.4
               ...
           EOF
           pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install
  ✗ CI workflow
      Fix: mkdir -p .github/workflows
           cat > .github/workflows/ci.yml <<'EOF' ...
  ...

  Result: 7/10 checks passed; 3 missing. Run 'st onboard -v' for details.

Out of scope (file separately):
  - 'st onboard --fix' to auto-apply fixes (risky; v1 leaves writes to the user)
  - Language-specific test scaffolding (Python pytest vs Node jest etc.) — onboard reports presence; doesn't generate
  - Per-rig override of which checks apply (e.g. 'this repo doesn't need GH Actions because it uses CircleCI')
acceptance_criteria:
- 'st onboard' runs from anywhere inside a rig (walks up to find .sietch/rig.config) and prints a pass/fail report
- Read-only by default — never mutates the rig or runs install commands without explicit '--fix' (out of scope for v1)
- Exit code 0 if all checks pass, 1 if any fail (suitable for CI-style usage)
- Each failed check prints a concrete copy-pasteable fix command/snippet
- Checks performed (in order):
  • .sietch/rig.config exists AND REPO_OWNER/REPO_NAME are not the example placeholders
  • .beads/ exists (bd is the canonical task tracker per CLAUDE.md)
  • gh CLI authenticated for REPO_SLUG (gh auth status -h github.com)
  • .pre-commit-config.yaml exists at repo root
  • pre-commit hooks actually installed (.git/hooks/pre-commit has the pre-commit-installed marker)
  • .github/workflows/ has at least one .yml/.yaml file
  • The first workflow runs on pull_request events (grep 'on:' block)
  • A test directory exists (tests/ or test/ at repo root)
  • At least one test file exists in that directory (test_*.py / *_test.py / *.test.{js,ts} / *_test.go)
  • WORKTREE_BASE is writable (try mkdir -p; rmdir)
- Verbose mode '-v' shows what each check tested and which path it inspected

title: cut empty-cycle token cost via lib/eligibility.sh + exponential backoff
description:
With 'st loop' running, the dev-agent / reviewer-orchestrator / dispatcher loops wake on every tick and burn tokens loading their 30+ kB system prompts just to discover there's no work to do, then exit. On a quiet repo this is the dominant cost — most ticks are empty.

Fix: do the eligibility check in pure shell BEFORE invoking 'claude --append-system-prompt …'. Only spin up the agent when there's at least one candidate. Stack exponential backoff on top so cycle frequency itself decays when the queue's been quiet.
design:
Files added/changed:
  - lib/eligibility.sh (new) — sourced by wrappers and invokable by agents via Bash
  - templates/rig.config.example — add EMPTY_CYCLE_BACKOFF_BASE_SECONDS, EMPTY_CYCLE_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS, eligibility cache dir
  - wrappers/run-developer.sh — preflight + early exit on empty
  - wrappers/run-reviewer.sh — preflight + early exit on empty
  - wrappers/run-loop.sh — backoff state per pane (~/.cache/sietch/<rig>/<mode>.empty_cycles)
  - templates/developer.md — replace ad-hoc 'gh issue list' with 'bash $SIETCH_HOME/lib/eligibility.sh dev'
  - templates/reviewer-orchestrator.md — same swap

Cache shape (last-seen state, used to detect 'nothing changed since last empty cycle'):
  ~/.cache/sietch/<repo_slug_safe>/<mode>.last-seen   # one-line digest, e.g. sha256 of sorted candidate IDs

Eligibility function contract (stdout = newline-delimited candidate IDs; exit 0 if any, exit 1 if none):
  count=$(eligibility_dev_count)
  if [ -z "$count" ]; then exit 1; fi

Out of scope (file separately):
  - Push-based triggering via GitHub webhooks (replace polling entirely) — bigger architectural shift
  - Sharing the cache across multiple panes/loops (race conditions; the per-pane local cache is enough for v1)
acceptance_criteria:
- New lib/eligibility.sh with one named function per agent mode:
  • eligibility_dev_count       — open severity:high|medium issues, no assignee, no in-flight dev-agent PR
  • eligibility_review_pending  — dev-agent PRs not yet reviewed at current headRefOid
  • eligibility_followup_pending — PRs with reviewer comment newer than dev-agent's last response
  • eligibility_conflict_pending — PRs with mergeStateStatus DIRTY on ${BRANCH_PREFIX}/* branches
- Each function reads rig.config (BRANCH_PREFIX, severity labels, etc.) and prints either an empty result or a list of candidate IDs/numbers + an exit code (0 = work, 1 = nothing)
- run-developer.sh / run-reviewer.sh / run-loop.sh dispatchers source the helper and short-circuit BEFORE invoking 'claude' when eligibility is empty
- Confirmed: empty-cycle invocation consumes zero LLM tokens (verified by running 'st dev' on a quiet repo and checking that no 'claude' subprocess fires)
- Each agent template ALSO calls the same function as its first step, so the in-prompt re-check stays in sync — drift impossible
- Exponential backoff on consecutive empty cycles: 60s → 120s → 240s → 480s, cap at ${EMPTY_CYCLE_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS:-300}, reset to base on first non-empty cycle. Implemented in run-loop.sh per-pane state file.
close_reason: Shipped at sha 9778e90: lib/eligibility.sh with dev/review predicates, wrapper preflight in run-developer.sh + run-reviewer.sh (exit 2 on no-work), exponential backoff in loop_dev_mode1 + loop_reviewer (60→120→240→300, capped via EMPTY_CYCLE_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS=300), Step 0 fast-gate in developer.md + reviewer-orchestrator.md. Smoke-tested on quiet ai-cfo-eval-harness rig — both wrappers exit 2 without spawning claude.

title: st init: write a SIETCH marker-block into the rig's CLAUDE.md
description:
Sietch currently has no programmatic way to communicate framework-specific guidance to a Claude session running inside a consumer rig. A human Claude session has no idea that the dev-agent owns 'BRANCH_PREFIX/*' branches, that locks live under LOCK_DIR, or which 'st *' commands are available — it has to be told manually each time, or the user has to hand-write the same boilerplate into every rig's CLAUDE.md.

Mirror bd's pattern: a marker-bracketed block in CLAUDE.md, written by 'st init' and refreshed by a future 'st sync'. Closes the onboarding loop — 'st init' writes rig.config AND the CLAUDE.md block, so a new rig is genuinely one-step.
design:
New template: templates/claude-md-block.md — parameterized, rendered through the existing lib/render-prompt.sh pipeline.

bin/st cmd_init extended: after copying rig.config from the example, render claude-md-block.md and either:
  - append it to existing CLAUDE.md (between markers, preserving the rest), OR
  - write a new CLAUDE.md containing only the block + a stub heading

Hash computed by piping rendered block (without marker lines) into 'shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-8' and substituted into the BEGIN marker.

Idempotency: a small awk/sed pass detects the BEGIN/END pair. If present, skip; if absent, append. (Refresh-when-hash-stale is the 'st sync' job.)

Out of scope (file separately if/when needed):
  - 'st sync' to refresh the block on framework upgrade
  - Auto-detection of stale blocks across rigs
  - Per-rig customization of block content (beyond rig.config substitutions)
acceptance_criteria:
- 'st init' writes a SIETCH marker-block into the rig's CLAUDE.md
- Creates CLAUDE.md if it doesn't exist; preserves all user content outside the block if it does
- Idempotent: re-running 'st init' does not duplicate the block; if a block exists, leaves it alone (refresh is the future 'st sync' job)
- Marker format mirrors bd: <!-- BEGIN SIETCH INTEGRATION v:1 hash:<sha8> --> … <!-- END SIETCH INTEGRATION -->
- Block content includes:
  • one-paragraph mental model (this rig is a sietch consumer; framework lives at ~/code/sietch)
  • command reference (st dev / st review / st loop start / st help)
  • coordinate-with-dev-agent rules (don't push to BRANCH_PREFIX/*, don't tamper with LOCK_DIR, dev-agent uses filesystem locks for atomic claim)
  • pointer to .sietch/rig.config for tunables
- Block is parameterized — rig.config variables (BRANCH_PREFIX, LOCK_DIR, etc.) substituted via the existing render-prompt.sh
- Block hash is sha256 of rendered content truncated to 8 chars (used by future 'st sync' for drift detection)
- AGENTS.md is NOT touched — bd's choice to write to both files is a redundancy we don't repeat

title: add 'st permissions install' to bootstrap user-level Claude grants
description:
When a new user installs sietch, Claude Code re-prompts them for every Bash/MCP grant the agents need (gh, git, bd, python, pre-commit, tmux, …). A self-contained 'st permissions install' command should remove that friction so onboarding a rig is genuinely one-step.

Migrated from ai-cfo-eval-harness-a4fi (filed there before this repo had its own bd workspace).
design:
Subcommand 'permissions' added to bin/st with dispatch to lib/permissions.sh.

Grant list lives in lib/permissions.json — single source of truth, readable by users.
Scope = grants the four sietch agents actually invoke; NOT personal QoL:
  gh *, git *, bd *, st *, python *, python3 *, pytest *,
  pre-commit run *, ruff *, tmux *, pkill *, kill *, bash, jq *, mkdir *, chmod *

Implementation:
  - lib/permissions.sh reads lib/permissions.json (jq parses)
  - Reads existing ~/.claude/settings.json (creates from template if missing)
  - Computes set difference (new - existing) using jq
  - On install: cp settings.json settings.json.sietch.bak; jq merge writes new file
  - On --dry-run: print the diff list (one entry per line)
  - On list: cat lib/permissions.json | jq '.allow'
  - Atomic write: jq → temp file → mv into place

Out of scope (file separately if needed):
  - Project-specific grants (e.g. .venv/, PYTHONPATH=src) — those still belong in repo's .claude/settings.local.json
  - 'st permissions uninstall' (revert to backup) — nice-to-have, not in v1
  - Auto-running install during 'st init' — keep explicit; user opts in
acceptance_criteria:
- 'st permissions install' merges sietch-required grants into ~/.claude/settings.json
- Idempotent: re-running adds nothing if all entries already present (compare by exact string match)
- '--dry-run' prints the diff (entries that would be added) and exits 0 without writing
- 'st permissions list' prints the grant list as JSON (no I/O on settings.json)
- A backup is written to ~/.claude/settings.json.sietch.bak before any modification
- New ~/.claude/ is handled: creates settings.json with {permissions: {allow: [...]}} if missing
- JSON is validated (jq -e .) before and after; refuses to write if pre-state is invalid
- Clear error if jq is missing on PATH ('install jq via brew install jq')
- Top-level non-permission keys (e.g. effortLevel, skipAutoPermissionPrompt) are preserved

title: refresh stale CLAUDE.md marker-block when framework upgrades (st sync vs implicit)
description:
Once sietch-byb ships and 'st init' writes a SIETCH marker-block with a content hash, rigs will go stale silently when ~/code/sietch is git-pulled and the template changes. Need a way to detect and refresh stale blocks.

DESIGN QUESTION (deliberately deferred until the first real stale-block moment): explicit 'st sync' command vs implicit refresh on every 'st *' invocation (the pattern bd uses). bd's implicit approach is ergonomically nicer — no command to remember, never out of date — but adds a cost (and a moving target) to every CLI call. Decide based on (a) how often templates actually change, (b) whether there's ever a multi-rig propagation pain.

Filed P4: don't build until there's evidence of need (a template change worth propagating across multiple rigs).
design:
Two paths to evaluate when this is built:

A) Explicit 'st sync':
   - bin/st adds 'sync' subcommand
   - lib/sync.sh: render template → hash → compare to rig's marker → if stale, replace block
   - User must remember to run after 'cd ~/code/sietch && git pull'

B) Implicit refresh:
   - Wrap every 'st *' subcommand entry in a stale-block check
   - On stale: print one-line notice + refresh + continue
   - Cache last-seen-template-hash in ~/.cache/sietch/ to keep the check cheap

Recommendation when building: start with B (matches bd's pattern; ergonomically cleaner) but only if multi-rig propagation is real. If single-rig is permanent, neither is worth building — just re-run 'st init --force-block-refresh' manually after big upgrades.

Out of scope:
  - Refreshing rig.config (different problem; user values must not be clobbered)
  - Cross-rig discovery (sietch doesn't track which rigs exist)
acceptance_criteria:
- Detect stale marker-block: compare hash in CLAUDE.md's BEGIN marker against fresh hash of rendered current template
- Refresh stale block in place, preserving all CLAUDE.md content outside the markers
- Picked design (explicit 'st sync' or implicit on every 'st *') is informed by actual usage, not guessed
- If implicit: refresh path adds no measurable latency to common commands (cache the hash check)
- If explicit: 'st sync' is idempotent (no-op when already current) and supports '--dry-run' to print the diff
